prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Try double-clicking your pet to toggle desktop companion controls!"]
1: ["Synthesizing pet personality & desk animations..."]
2: ["Set Your Pet Quick Controls", "Choose a quick desktop shortcut to call or hide your pet whenever you need to focus.", "Set Call/Hide Shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+P)"]
3: ["Initializing desktop physics and sprite assets..."]
4: ["Choose Your Companion Experience", "Select whether your pet roams your desktop or guides you through story mode."]
5: ["Master Desktop Docking", "Drag your pet to the edge of your screen or taskbar to dock it out of the way."]
6: ["Welcome Back or Get Started", "Sign in to restore your existing desktop pets or create a new sync account."]
7: ["Your pet is now active on your desktop! Click to open quick commands."]
8: ["Fun Fact: Your desktop pet will occasionally nap on active app windows!"]
9: ["How Desktop Pets Work", "Desktop pets live quietly on your screen, react to your work breaks, and keep you company throughout the day.", "Choose My Companion Path"]
